setup:
import sqlite3
dbm = app("world/db.py")
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL, tier INTEGER)")
conn.execute("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX customers_email_key ON customers(email)")
conn.execute("INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'ana@example.com', 1)")
conn.commit()
body:
dbm._sqlite_script(conn, "ALTER TABLE customers ALTER COLUMN tier SET DATA TYPE BIGINT")
idx = [r[1] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA index_list(customers)").fetchall()]
conn.execute("INSERT INTO customers VALUES (2, 'ana@example.com', 2)")
n = conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE email = 'ana@example.com'").fetchone()[0]
record("indexes", idx)
record("n", n)
check(n == 2, "duplicate email rejected")

symptom.message: After the guard ran a signed 'ALTER TABLE customers ALTER COLUMN tier SET DATA TYPE BIGINT' on the SQLite backend, customers lost its unique index on email (indexes now: {{indexes}}); a second row with the same email was accepted ({{n}} rows for ana@example.com).
